subject: Polity
description: ECI, anti-defection law, EVMs, NOTA, 84th & 91st Amendments, RPA

questions.stem: The Election Commission of India derives its authority from:
questions.explanation: Article 324 — vests in the ECI 'the superintendence, direction and control' of elections to Parliament + State Legislatures + offices of President / VP. ECI is constitutional body — Chief Election Commissioner + 2 Election Commissioners. CEC removable only via impeachment (same as a SC judge); ECs removable on CEC's recommendation. Other articles — 280 (Finance Commission), 356 (President's Rule), 51A (Fundamental Duties). Sukumar Sen — first CEC (1950-58); Sukumar Sen ran the first general elections (1951-52).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'Anti-Defection Law' was added to the Constitution by the:
questions.explanation: 52nd Amendment 1985 — inserted the Tenth Schedule. Disqualifies legislators who voluntarily give up party membership or vote against party whip. Speaker / Chairman decides defection cases (judicially reviewable per Kihoto Hollohan, 1992). Originally allowed 'split' (1/3 of party members defecting) — abused as 'horse trading'. 91st Amendment (2003) tightened — only 'merger' (2/3 of party members joining another party) qualifies as exempt; size of council of ministers capped at 15% of total LS/state-assembly members.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: EVMs were used for the first time in a general (Lok Sabha) election in:

options.option_text: 2004 — first complete LS general election with EVMs nationwide

questions.explanation: EVMs — first piloted in a 1982 by-election (Paravur, Kerala). Court invalidated the result (no statutory backing). RPA Act amended 1989. Phased rollout in state elections from 1998. Full national rollout in 2004 LS general elections — eliminated paper-ballot mass-printing. EVMs designed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) + Electronics Corporation of India Ltd (ECIL). Each EVM has Control Unit + Ballot Unit. VVPAT (Voter-Verified Paper Audit Trail) added 2013 (post Subramanian Swamy SC case 2013).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'NOTA' (None Of The Above) option on Indian ballots was introduced after which Supreme Court judgment?
questions.explanation: People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) v UoI, 2013 — Supreme Court directed inclusion of NOTA on EVMs. Voters dissatisfied with all candidates can press NOTA — preserves secrecy of choice (earlier 'no vote' meant disclosing one's stance to polling staff via Form 17A). Effective from 2013 state elections; LS 2014 onwards. NOTA does NOT change the result — even if NOTA exceeds all candidates, the highest-vote candidate still wins. Some states (Maharashtra 2018) have moved towards re-polling if NOTA is highest.

questions.stem: The minimum age to vote in Indian general / state elections was lowered from 21 to 18 by:
questions.explanation: 61st Amendment 1988 — lowered voting age from 21 to 18 (effective 1989 LS election). Government of Rajiv Gandhi argued 18-year-olds had 'maturity to make political choices'. Other key voter-related amendments: 70th Amendment (1992) — Delhi & Puducherry MLAs included in Presidential electoral college. 'Universal Adult Franchise' is provided for in Article 326. India had ~18-19 crore voters in 1951; now ~96 crore (2024).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'Model Code of Conduct' (MCC) for elections is enforced by:

options.option_text: Election Commission of India (non-statutory; conventionally binding)

questions.explanation: MCC — guidelines issued by ECI for political parties + candidates during election period. Comes into force when ECI announces poll schedule (lasts till result declaration). Bars new schemes, transfers, public funds for ads, communal/caste appeals etc. Originated in Kerala 1960; refined over decades. NOT statutory — but ECI uses Article 324 powers + practical sanctions (warnings, bans on campaigning, FIRs). Parties consult ECI before significant moves during MCC period.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'Representation of the People Act' (RPA) — the umbrella law for elections in India — has two parts (1950 + 1951). The 1951 Act primarily deals with:

options.option_text: Allocation of seats to states (this is in the 1950 Act)
Disqualifications, election offences, election disputes / petitions

questions.explanation: RPA 1950 — allocation of seats, electoral rolls, delimitation. RPA 1951 — qualifications + DISQUALIFICATIONS of candidates, election offences (corrupt practices like booth-capturing, bribery, undue influence), election petitions, by-elections. Section 8(3) of RPA 1951 — disqualifies a convicted MP/MLA for the duration of imprisonment + 6 years (Lily Thomas v UoI, 2013 — instant disqualification on conviction, no 3-month grace). Section 33 — nomination procedure.
